editorial.headline: The Wholesale Honey Trade Open Nationally but Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This broad wholesale category is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks it because its Large-scale scopes are Low or Medium-Low risk.
editorial.body:
This is a wholesale activity with a sharp geographic divide. At the national level, it is open to foreign investment and carries a 100% maximum foreign-ownership ceiling. In Bali, however, a foreign investor cannot register the activity under PMA today. The decisive fact is Bali’s permanent, island-wide bar on PMA registration for activities assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk. The Bali rationale for this activity cites that moratorium in May 2026.

The activity itself concerns wholesale food and beverage products derived from animal husbandry and fisheries. It is a broad category, intended to take in qualifying trade that has not been set out elsewhere within its classification. The record gives two useful anchors: wholesale honey from beekeeping, and honey collected from forests. These examples keep the centre of gravity clear. The subject is wholesale commerce in animal- and fishery-derived foods and drinks, with honey specifically named as an illustration.

That breadth does not confine the activity to a particular company size. Registration is open across every scale in the record—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. For a nationally registered PMA company, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the stated ceiling is 100%. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In other words, the national entry permits foreign ownership up to its full stated limit; it does not place a lower foreign-share cap on this activity.

Bali reverses the practical answer for PMA registration. The local status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO, and the reason is unusually direct: at the Besar scale, every scope is rated Rendah or Menengah-Rendah. Under the Bali rule cited in the record, all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI are blocked for PMA, across the island and permanently. So the national 100% ceiling is real, but it is not a route to PMA registration in Bali. It tells you the ownership position nationally; the Bali moratorium determines whether a PMA filing can be made there, and for this activity the answer is no.
editorial.pullQuote: The national 100% ceiling is real, but it is not a route to PMA registration in Bali.
